nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and every family $A_1, \dots, A_{100}$ of cubes in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ (not necessarily distinct), that is, images of $\{0, 1\}^n$ under linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$, the sumset $A_1 + \dots + A_{100}$ is all of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$.
nodes.title: Any $100$ cubes sum to all of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$

nodes.summary: The statement that for every $n \ge 1$ and every family $A_1, \dots, A_{100}$ of cubes in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ (not necessarily distinct), that is, images of $\{0, 1\}^n$ under linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$, the sumset $A_1 + \dots + A_{100}$ is all of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$.
nodes.title: Green's problem on sums of $100$ cubes in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the standard cube is the set $\{0, 1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{F}_3^n$ of vectors each of whose coordinates is $0$ or $1$.
nodes.title: The standard cube in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$

nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_3^n$ is a cube if there is an $\mathbb{F}_3$-linear automorphism $e$ of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ with $A = e(\{0, 1\}^n)$, the image of the standard cube $\{0, 1\}^n$ under $e$.
nodes.title: Cubes in $\mathbb{F}_3^n$

nodes.summary: For sets $A_1, \dots, A_{100} \subseteq \mathbb{F}_3^n$, the property that every $v \in \mathbb{F}_3^n$ can be written as $v = a_1 + \dots + a_{100}$ with $a_i \in A_i$ for each $i$, that is, $A_1 + \dots + A_{100} = \mathbb{F}_3^n$.
nodes.title: A sumset of $100$ sets equal to $\mathbb{F}_3^n$
